vedic_reference.note: श्रुति शब्दात् । श्रुतिः वेदाः (Shruti shabdat. Shruti hi Vedah.) - The Vedas are called Shruti because they are heard, not written.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shrutisha, meaning 'one who hears the sacred sacred/divine teachings,' highlights the importance of listening and learning in Hindu culture, particularly in relation to spiritual practices and the teachings of the Vedas and other religious texts. It emphasizes the importance of gaining knowledge through both hearing and direct experience.
data.spiritual_significance: This name is deeply significant from a spiritual perspective as it reflects the idea of being a vessel for the divine teachings, a conduit for the sacred knowledge that comes from the universe and from the guru. It also signifies the importance of remaining open, curious, and receptive to the universe and to the divine wisdom that is always available to us, and of actively seeking out wisdom and knowledge to deepen our spiritual practice and understanding. Additionally, it reminds us of the power of the spoken word and the importance of honoring the words of our gurus and spiritual texts as sacred and transformative.

historical_references.reference: Shrutisha was an ancient Indian sage and scholar, known for her deep knowledge and wisdom in the Vedas and Upanishads. She is believed to have lived during the late Vedic period, around 1000 BCE.
Shrutisha is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, an epic Sanskrit poem, as one of the seventy-two great sages who was present at the assembly called the Sabha Parva.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shrutisha, which means 'that which is heard or listened to in the heart', is gaining popularity in modern contexts. On Facebook, it is used by individuals who identify with the name and wish to connect with like-minded people. On LinkedIn, it is seen as a unique and meaningful name for professional profiles. On YouTube, Shrutisha is a popular name among channels dedicated to self-improvement and spiritual growth, where listeners can immerse themselves in the teachings and wisdom of ancient Hindu texts and practices.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Shrutisha, a teacher in Mumbai, India, shares that their name Shrutisha meaning "One who has heard" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Shrutisha: The radiant embodiment of sacred knowledge and wisdom, whose ears are ever open to the divine hymns and teachings.
